en.title: Wanda Maximoff Proves She's the True Anchor of the MCU
en.summary: VisionQuest's finale might have focused on Vision, but a surprise post-credits scene shifted all attention back to the Scarlet Witch. It seems even the show's star knew this was inevitable.
en.body:
A strange thing happened when **VisionQuest** wrapped its first season. The Disney+ series, spearheaded by **Terry Matalas**, delivered a compelling narrative centered on the synthezoid **Vision** ( **Paul Bettany**) and his volatile creator **Ultron** ( **James Spader**). It explored profound questions about life and existence, boasted strong chemistry between its leads, and even managed to surpass its predecessor, **WandaVision**, in certain aspects. Yet, as a surprise post-credits sequence played, revealing **Doctor Doom** ( **Robert Downey Jr.**) resurrecting **Wanda Maximoff** ( **Elizabeth Olsen**) for a future **Avengers: Doomsday**, the conversation irrevocably shifted. Suddenly, all eyes were on the Scarlet Witch.

This pivot was perhaps anticipated by the show's own star. In an exit interview with The Playlist, **Paul Bettany** admitted he actively discouraged Marvel Studios head **Kevin Feige** from including Olsen in the series. "I really don’t think you should distract from [Vision] by giving the audience that at the end of the [show]," Bettany stated. "It will just fundamentally all become about WandaVision again, and this should and can stand on its own." While Bettany was correct that **VisionQuest** ultimately stood on its own merits, he was also prescient about the magnetic pull of Wanda Maximoff. Her presence, even in absence, proved she remains a foundational anchor for the entire Marvel Cinematic Universe.

## The Unshakeable Pull of the Scarlet Witch

Wanda Maximoff's journey from a Silver Age mutant with hex powers to a reality-warping cosmic entity has been one of the most transformative arcs in the MCU. Her initial appearances in comics were alongside her brother **Quicksilver** as part of the Brotherhood of Evil Mutants, wielding powers that were often reactive. Over decades, however, her abilities evolved dramatically, culminating in the powerful, grief-fueled Scarlet Witch we've seen in the MCU. **WandaVision** itself was a masterclass in character exploration, delving into her psyche through decades of sitcom tropes. Despite the focus on Vision's quest for identity and his confrontation with Ultron, the narrative always seemed to circle back to Wanda's influence and emotional impact, a testament to the character's deep resonance with audiences.

## Why This Matters to Fans

For dedicated fans, the enduring appeal of **Wanda Maximoff** isn't just about her immense power; it's about her complex emotional journey and her pivotal role in shaping the MCU's present and future. Her connection to **Vision** is one of the most compelling relationships in the franchise, and her status as a near-omnipotent being makes her a crucial player in any major cosmic threat. The ending of **VisionQuest**, while seemingly setting up new storylines, ultimately reinforces that no matter the focus of a given series or film, Wanda's narrative thread is inextricably woven into the fabric of the MCU. Her resurrection by **Doctor Doom** signals her central importance in upcoming multiversal conflicts, leaving fans eager to see how her story unfolds next.

## What's Next

With **Wanda Maximoff** officially back in the fold and seemingly under the influence of **Doctor Doom**, her next appearance is highly anticipated. While specific details regarding her role in **Avengers: Doomsday** or other upcoming projects have not yet been announced, her resurrection confirms her continued significance. Fans can expect her influence to be felt across the MCU as the Multiverse Saga progresses.

content_raw: This post contains spoilers for VisionQuest season 1 episode 8 A strange thing happened when VisionQuest finished. The Disney+ series created by Star Trek: Picard showrunner Terry Matalas told a largely enjoyable story about the synthezoid Vision ( Paul Bettany ) and his maniacal robot creator Ultron ( James Spader ) as they found themselves and debated the nature of life. It had incredible chemistry between the leads, some fun setpieces, and even ended on a stronger note than its predecessor, WandaVision . Yet, as soon as a surprise post-credits sequence played , revealing Doctor Doom ( Robert Downey Jr. ) resurrecting Wanda Maximoff ( Elizabeth Olsen ) in preparation for Avengers: Doomsday , all anyone could talk about was Wanda. In an exit interview with The Playlist , Paul Bettany sure sounds like he expected that to happen. When asked about the possibility of having Olsen reprise her role for the series, Bettany reveals that he dissuaded Kevin Feige from including her. “I really don’t think you should distract from [Vision] by giving the audience that at the end of the [show],” he said. “It will just fundamentally all become about WandaVision again, and this should and can stand on its own.” And he was right, not that VisionQuest became WandaVision , but that everything became about Wanda—because Wanda Maximoff is an anchor of the MCU . Looking back on the history of Wanda Maximoff, her current status does come as a surprise. The Scarlet Witch first appeared in 1964’s X-Men #4, by Jack Kirby and Stan Lee, alongside her twin brother Quicksilver as a member of the Brotherhood of Evil Mutants. Like most female characters in the Silver Age, she had inherently defensive powers, the ability to cast hexes which gave people bad luck. A year later, she and Quicksilver graduated to the Avengers, where Captain American recruited them to join fellow former criminal Hawkeye in a lineup dubbed “Cap’s Kooky Quartet.” In the pages of Avengers and West Coast Avengers , Wanda became defined more by her drama and relationships than by her powers. She was courted by Hawkeye, and dated both Vision and Wonder Man, leading to lots of soap opera moments. While she did receive training from the crone Agatha Harkness, even her power boost was mostly served to advance her relationships, as when she created the twins Tommy and Billy as children for her and Vision. Worse yet, Marvel time and again associated Wanda’s power boosts with evil, having her go crazy several times, wiping out the Avengers and the X-Men. The MCU has treated Wanda better, but not by much. After a post-credits tease in Captain America: The Winter Soldier , she and her twin Pietro (Aaron Taylor-Johnson) debut in Avengers: Age of Ultron , where Wanda mostly uses her powers to give people cameo-laden nightmares.
